questions.q: What does `public with sharing class ServiceContractEvaluator` mean for how this class queries data?
options: It ignores the running user's sharing rules and sees all records
It can only be called from asynchronous Apex
It disables governor limits for this class
It enforces the running user's sharing rules and record-level access when it queries
questions.explain: with sharing enforces the running user's sharing rules and record-level access, the opposite of without sharing, which is the right default for a class other automation might call.

questions.q: Why does `isClaimCovered` take an `Id` and a `Decimal` as parameters instead of a whole `Warranty_Claim__c` record?
options: Apex methods cannot accept sObject parameters
To keep the method reusable by anything that has an Asset Id and an amount, not tied to one specific object
Decimal parameters run faster than sObject parameters
Because Warranty_Claim__c does not have an Asset lookup field
questions.explain: Taking primitive parameters keeps the method reusable by any caller with an Asset Id and an amount -- the Lesson 9 trigger and a future LWC alike -- rather than coupling it to one specific record type.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the correct bulk-safe pattern for evaluating many Assets at once, instead of calling a single-Id query method in a loop?
options: Collect the Ids into a Set<Id> and run one query filtering with an IN clause
Call the method once per record inside a for loop regardless of record count
Use a while loop with a hardcoded limit of 200
Always use without sharing to speed up the query
questions.explain: Bulk-safe code collects Ids into a Set<Id> and queries once with WHERE Asset__c IN :assetIds, rather than issuing one query per record in a loop.

questions.q: Per this lesson's cited governor limits, how many SOQL queries are allowed in a synchronous Apex transaction, and how many records can SOQL retrieve across that transaction?
options: 10 queries, 1,000 records
500 queries, 10,000 records
100 queries, 50,000 records
Unlimited queries, 50,000 records
questions.explain: The current Apex Developer Guide sets synchronous transactions at up to 100 SOQL queries and a maximum of 50,000 records retrieved by SOQL across the transaction.

questions.q: What exception does Apex throw when a transaction exceeds a governor limit?
options: NullPointerException
LimitException
DmlException
QueryException
questions.explain: Exceeding a governor limit throws a LimitException, which stops the transaction -- the reason bulk-safe patterns like querying outside loops matter.
